rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every female descended from a person by birth at any number of generations, through male or female links, counts as his daughter; this prohibition is permanent.
rows.anchor: كل أنثى رجع نسبها إليك بالولادة بدرجة أو درجات بإناث أو ذكور فهن بنتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition of daughters and sisters is everlasting; neither category has ever become lawful.
rows.anchor: وتحريم هاتين مؤبد لم تزالا، ولم تحلا قط لأحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sister is any female born to someone whom one of one's parents bore in the first degree.
rows.anchor: كل أنثى ولدها شخص ولدك في الدرجة الأولى فهي أختك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A paternal aunt is the sister of any male ancestor; this also includes the sister of one's maternal grandfather.
rows.anchor: وكل ذكر رجع نسبك إليه فأخته عمتك، وقد تكون العمة من جهة الأم، وهي أخت أبي أمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scope of nieces through brothers and sisters matches that of one's own daughter, and these women are forbidden through lineage and kinship.
rows.anchor: والتحديد في بنات الأخ وبنات الأخت كالتحديد في بنت الصلب، وهؤلاء محرمات بالأنساب والأرحام

rows.speaker: المفسرون وأهل العلم
rows.claim: Women forbidden through lineage and kinship are absolutely forbidden and never lawful; women made forbidden by a later circumstance, listed in the rest of the verse, are not in that category.
rows.anchor: كل امرأة حرم الله نكاحها للنسب والرحم فتحريمها مبهم، والمبهمة لا تحل بوجه من الوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nursing mothers are called mothers as a matter of prohibition, just as the Prophet's wives are called the mothers of believers.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء سمين أمهات للحرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A woman whose milk relationship connects her to the nursed person is a mother, including the woman who nursed that person's mother or father.
rows.anchor: وكل أنثى انتسبت باللبن إليها فهي أمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Milk kinship creates a marriage prohibition only after five separate nursing sessions.
rows.anchor: أن يكون خمس رضعات

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet states that nursing after the first two years creates no prohibition; al-Wahidi makes the two-year period the second condition for milk kinship.
rows.anchor: لقوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: "لا رضاع بعد الحولين"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There are three milk-sister relationships: a shared milk mother and father, a shared milk father, or a shared milk mother with milk from another man.
rows.anchor: وأخوات الرضاعة ثلاث الأولى: أختك لأبيك وأمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A milk mother and milk sister would not be forbidden absent nursing; nursing makes their prohibition permanent, placing them among the absolutely forbidden.
rows.anchor: لولا الرضاعة لم يحرما، وكان الرضاع تحريمها

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet's rule that breastfeeding prohibits the same relationships as lineage does.
rows.anchor: وروت عائشة رضي الله عنها، عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: "يحرم من الرضاعة ما يحرم من النسب"

rows.speaker: أولو التحقيق من ذوي العلم
rows.claim: The verse itself indicates the hadith's limit: it names mothers and sisters, covering birth and sibling routes through which all seven lineage-prohibited categories arise.
rows.anchor: وقال أولو التحقيق من ذوي العلم: إن الحد الذي ذكره رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في حديث عائشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wife's mother is forbidden as soon as her daughter is contracted in marriage, whether by milk or lineage, because the verse states the ban without a consummation condition; this is today's consensus.
rows.anchor: فهي حرام عليك بنفس العقد على ابنتها؛ لأن الله تعالى أطلق التحريم ولم يقيده بالدخول. هذا إجماع الأمة اليوم

rows.speaker: علي وزيد وابن عمر وابن الزبير وجابر وابن عباس
rows.claim: A group of Companions held that a wife's mother becomes forbidden only after consummation with the daughter, as with a stepdaughter.
rows.anchor: وكان جماعة من الصحابة يذهبون إلى أن المرأة إنما تحرم بالدخول بالبنت، كالربيبة إنما تحرم بالدخول بأمها

rows.speaker: علي وزيد وابن عمر وابن الزبير وجابر وابن عباس
rows.claim: They construed the consummation clause as applying to both stepdaughters and mothers-in-law, so a mother-in-law would not be forbidden if her daughter was not entered upon.
rows.anchor: وهؤلاء يجعلون قول: {من نسائكم اللاتي دخلتم بهن فإن لم تكونوا دخلتم بهن} منتظما للربائب وأمهات النساء

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi prefers the majority view: the Prophet distinguishes the cases, forbidding a wife's mother upon marriage but allowing the daughter if the marriage to her mother ended before intercourse.
rows.anchor: إذا نكح الرجل المرأة فلا يحل له أن يتزوج أمها، دخل بالبنت أو لم يدخل

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata says a man who contracts with a woman and divorces her without seeing or having intercourse with her may not marry her mother.
rows.anchor: قال: لا هي مرسلة، دخل بها أو لم يدخل

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: After initially permitting marriage to a former wife's mother when no intercourse occurred, Ibn Masud found Medina's scholars opposed and ordered the man to leave her on returning to Kufa.
rows.anchor: فلما رجع إلى الكوفة لم يدخل داره حتى حضر ذلك الرجل وقرع عليه الباب، وأمره بالنزول عن تلك المرأة

rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: The verse's structure indicates that the consummation condition belongs only to stepdaughters: ordinary Arabic would describe a wife's mother as the mother of the wife one entered upon, not as being from one's entered-upon wives.
rows.anchor: في نظم هذه الآية دليل على أن الشرط بالدخول مختص به الربائب دون أمهات النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because “from your women” is unnecessary for the meaning of “mothers of your women,” it cannot be the condition or its coordinate; the condition is restricted to stepdaughters.
rows.anchor: من نسائي ومن امرأتي زيادة لا حاجة بقيام المعنى إليها

rows.speaker: محمد بن يزيد بن عبد الأكبر
rows.claim: Abu al-Abbas says the consummation phrase modifies only the women who are mothers of stepdaughters; consensus makes a stepdaughter lawful when her mother was not consummated with.
rows.anchor: قوله: {اللاتي دخلتم بهن} نعت للنساء اللواتي من أمهات الربائب لا غير

rows.speaker: محمد بن يزيد بن عبد الأكبر
rows.claim: If the phrase modified mothers-in-law, stepdaughters would be left unrestricted and would wrongly remain forbidden even without consummation with their mother.
rows.anchor: فمن أجاز أن يكون قوله تعالى: {من نسائكم اللاتي دخلتم بهن} نعتا لقوله: {وأمهات نسائكم} بقيت الربائب مطلقة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj supports Abu al-Abbas: when two grammatical referents have different predicates, one adjective cannot modify both, as the Arabic example demonstrates.
rows.anchor: والدليل على أن ما قال أبو العباس هو الصحيح أن الخبرين إذا اختلفا لم يكن نعتهما واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A stepdaughter is a man's wife's daughter by another man; she is so named because the man raises her.
rows.anchor: الربائب جمع الربيبة، وهي بنت امرأة الرجل من غيره، ومعناها: مربوبة؛ لأن الرجل هو يربيها

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Asma'i gives several forms of the verb for raising a child, all with the same meaning.
rows.anchor: يقال: رببت فلانا أربه، ورببته أرببه، وربيته أربيه، وربته فأنا أربته. كله معنى واحد

rows.speaker: شاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses مرببة as evidence for the word's sense of a girl being raised; the source does not identify the poet.
rows.anchor: وذاك له إذا العنقاء صارت ... مرببة وشب ابن الخصي

rows.speaker: راجز
rows.claim: An unnamed rajaz poet supplies تربيت as lexical evidence in the discussion of the root for upbringing; the source does not name him.
rows.anchor: والقبر صهر ضامن زميت ... ليس لمن ضمنه تربيت

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: “In your care” means the stepdaughters whom you have raised; حجر is plural and has both fatḥa and kasra pronunciations, according to Ibn al-Sikkit.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: يقول: اللاتي ربيتموهن في حجوركم. وهي جمع حجر

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: Being in a guardian's lap means being under his care and upbringing: sitting a child in one's lap became a figure for raising a child, like being in someone's custody.
rows.anchor: أي في ضمانكم وتربيتكم، ويقال: فلان في حجر فلان، إذا كان يلي تربيته

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda interprets “in your care” as “in your homes.”
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: {في حجوركم} أي: في بيوتكم

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari says being in someone's حجر means being under that person's protection and care.
rows.anchor: ويقال: فلان في حجر فلان، أي: في كنفه ومنعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A stepdaughter's descent through the wife is measured like a daughter's descent through the man, and she becomes forbidden only through intercourse with her mother, by consensus.
rows.anchor: وحد الربيبة في رجوعها إلى زوجتك مثل حد بنتك في رجوعها إليك، وهي لا تحرم بمجرد العقد على الأم

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth says a husband and wife are each called ḥalīl because they dwell in one place; its plural is ḥalāʾil.
rows.anchor: قال الليث: الحليل والحليلة الزوج والمرأة

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda derives the word from each spouse being alongside the other; anyone who lives beside or with someone is that person's ḥalīl.
rows.anchor: سميا بذلك؛ لأن كل واحد منهما يحال صاحبه

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda cites an unnamed poet's use of حليلته for a female neighbor, not a wife, because she lives alongside the man.
rows.anchor: لم يرد بالحليلة ههنا امرأته، إنما أراد جارته؛ لأنها تحاله في المنزل

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Another explanation derives the wife's name from each spouse loosening the other's garment, in the sense that the spouse is lawful; حليل is formed like صحيح from صحّ.
rows.anchor: ويقال: إنما سميت الزوجة حليلة؛ لأن كل واحد منهما يحل إزار صاحبه، على معنى أنه يحل له

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj interprets حليلة as محلة, a woman made lawful, from حلال.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: حليلة: يعني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation again derives the spouses' name from each loosening the other's garment.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لأن كل واحد منهما يحل إزاره صاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Of your loins” excludes adopted sons, who in early Islam had the status of biological sons.
rows.anchor: فيه احتراز عن المتبنى، وكان المتبنى في صدر الإسلام بمنزلة الابن

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata says a man may marry the wife of a son he adopted but who is not his biological son; the Prophet married Zayd ibn Haritha's former wife, prompting criticism and revelation.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء: وليس يحرم عليك حليلة ابن ادعيته

rows.speaker: أهل العلم
rows.claim: The wife of a milk-son is forbidden like the wife of a biological son, based on the Prophet's rule that milk kinship has the same prohibitions as lineage.
rows.anchor: قال أهل العلم: وحليلة الابن من الرضاع ملحقة في التحريم بحليلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A son's wife's prohibition begins with the marriage contract, as does the prohibition of one's father's wife; there is no disagreement on this.
rows.anchor: وهذا التحريم يحصل بنفس العقد، كحليلة الأب لا خلاف في هذا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Asked whether the son had consummated the marriage, Ibn Abbas answered, “Leave ambiguous what God left ambiguous.”
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: أبهموا ما أبهم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi explains that here “ambiguous” denotes a categorical prohibition with no permissible route, whether or not the son consummated the marriage; it is unlike a ban tied to a later circumstance.
rows.anchor: هذا من المبهم، أي: مما لا وجه فيه غير التحريم، سواء دخل بهن أو لم يدخل بهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “that you combine two sisters” is grammatically nominative because it means “combining two sisters” and coordinates with what precedes.
rows.anchor: أن في محل الرفع؛ لأنه بمعنى: والجمع بين الأختين، عطف على ما قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A man may not marry two sisters together, whether related by lineage or nursing.
rows.anchor: ويحرم على الرجل أن يجمع في النكاح أختين بالنسب أو باللبن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two enslaved sisters may be jointly owned, but intercourse with one makes the other forbidden until the first is relinquished by sale, gift, manumission, or a manumission contract.
rows.anchor: ويجوز الجمع بين أختين أمتين بملك اليمين، فإذا وطئ إحداهما حرمت الثانية عليه

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata interprets “what has passed” as practices of earlier peoples: Jacob combined Leah, mother of Judah, and Rachel, mother of Joseph; it was formerly lawful, then forbidden to this community out of mercy because of women's jealousy.
rows.anchor: وكان فيما مضى حلالا لجميع الأمم

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi, in Asbat's transmission, shares Ata's explanation that the exception refers to an earlier practice later prohibited.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول السدي في رواية أسباط

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the exception concerns what you did in pre-Islamic times, for which you are not held accountable after Islam.
rows.anchor: مضى منكم في الجاهلية فلا، تؤاخذون به بعد الإسلام

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil agrees with al-Kalbi and says people used to marry two sisters together; Abu Ishaq prefers this interpretation.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل في قوله: {إلا ما قد سلف} قال: لأنهم كانوا يجمعون بينهما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says pre-Islamic Arabs observed God's prohibitions except for marrying a man's father's wife and marrying two sisters together.
rows.anchor: كان أهل الجاهلية يحرمون ما حرم الله إلا امرأة الأب والجمع بين الأختين

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq paraphrases the exception as: what has already passed is forgiven.
rows.anchor: المعنى: سوى ما سلف فإنه مغفور لكم

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr calls the exception disconnected: إِلَّا means “but,” so prior cases are forgiven; he links the construction to 2:150.
rows.anchor: وهذا من الاستثناء المنقطع {إلا} بمعنى: لكن، كأنه قيل: لكن ما قد سلف فأنتم غير مؤاخذين به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seven categories are forbidden by lineage; the cause-based categories are nursing (mothers and sisters) and marriage affinity (wife's mother, father's wife, son's wife, and stepdaughters), with the father's wife named at 4:22.
rows.anchor: المحرمات بالنسب سبعة أصناف، ذكرت نسقا في أول الآية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والكلبي
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Kalbi, and others explain كتبنا as “We prescribed” or “made obligatory.”
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس والكلبي وغيرهما: يريد فرضنا وأوجبنا عليهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the command would have been imposed on the Jews and Arabs.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: يعني: على اليهود والعرب

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators say Israelites were commanded to kill themselves and emigrants to leave their homes; had the same been prescribed for the people addressed, only a few would have done it.
rows.anchor: كتب الله على بني إسرائيل أن يقتلوا أنفسهم، وكتب على المهاجرين أن يخرجوا من ديارهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads “only a few” as God's foreknowledge: only those whom He already knew would do so would act, as in Noah's story.
rows.anchor: أخبر عن علمه فيهم، كقوله عن نوح

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata identifies the few as the Helpers of Medina.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء: {إلا قليل منهم} يريد الأنصار

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil names Ammar ibn Yasir, Ibn Masud, and Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammās among the few.
rows.anchor: كان من القليل عمار بن ياسر، وابن مسعود، وثابت بن قيس بن شماس

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the verse was revealed about Thabit ibn Qays, who declared he would kill himself if God commanded it; Thabit was one of the few.
rows.anchor: نزلت في ثابت بن قيس؛ لأنه قال: إن الله يعلم لو أمرني بأمر أقتل نفسي لقتلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi prefers al-Hasan's reading: the exception is from those actually commanded, namely hypocrites and people whose faith was not settled, as indicated by 4:60 and 4:65.
rows.anchor: والظاهر في هذه الآية ما قال الحسن؛ لكون المستثنى من المكتوب عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi also allows a reading in which Jews, hypocrites, and believers are all addressed, the Companions are excepted, and the following clause refers to Jews and hypocrites.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أن قوله: {ولو أنا كتبنا عليهم} يريد اليهود والمنافقين والمؤمنين جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an sometimes has passages read as general and others as particular.
rows.anchor: وقد ورد في التنزيل آي حمل بعضها على العموم وبعضها على الخصوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative reading of إلا قليل منهم is preferred if the excluded and excepted groups differ: the commanded group is hypocrites and the exception is the Helpers, two distinct classes.
rows.anchor: أن يحمل على قراءة من قرأ {إلا قليل منهم} بالنصب

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says what they are admonished with is the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: ما يوعظون به من القرآن

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says it means what they are commanded to do.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: ما يؤمرون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Doing what they are admonished with would be better for them in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {لكان خيرا لهم} في الآخرة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says it would be better for them in their religion.
rows.anchor: لكان خيرا لهم في دينهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says it would protect them and better shield them from devils.
rows.anchor: لكان خيرا له في العصمة وأمنع من الشياطين

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ata, transmitting from Ibn Abbas, interprets “firmer” as firmer in their religion.
rows.anchor: أشد تثبيتا في دينهم

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil interprets “firmer” as affirming God's command.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: {وأشد تثبيتا} تصديقا بأمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi explains Ata's point: obeying the Messenger would give them greater firmness in religion.
rows.anchor: لو أطاعوا الرسول كان ذلك أشد تثبيتا منهم لأنفسهم في الدين

rows.speaker: أبو روق
rows.claim: Abu Rawq glosses تثبيتا as making something established or verified.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو روق: {تثبيتا} تحقيقا

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ata from Ibn Abbas says God would guide them to an upright religion, namely the religion of Abrahamic monotheism rather than Judaism.
rows.anchor: يريد دين الحنيفية لا دين اليهودية

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that God would continually grant them the subtle grace that steadies them in obedience and on the straight path, like the prayer in 1:6.
rows.anchor: ولأدمنا لهم اللطيفة التي يثبتون بها على الطاعة في لزوم الطريق المستقيم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view takes the guidance as leading them on the path to Paradise in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ولهديناهم في الآخرة طريق الجنة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية الكلبي
rows.claim: One occasion report says the verse came about Thawban, who grieved at separation from the Prophet and feared being unable to meet him in the afterlife because the Prophet would rank above him.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول ابن عباس في رواية الكلبي

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says some Helpers asked how they could see the Prophet in Paradise, since he would dwell in its highest place and they longed for him; the verse then came down.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: إن ناسا من الأنصار

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi reports an Ansari who loved the Prophet more than family and possessions, feared dying without seeing him in Paradise, and wept; after the verse, the Prophet told him to rejoice.
rows.anchor: لأنت أحب إلي من نفسي وأهلي ومالي وولدي، ولولا أني آتيك فأراك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says believers feared that the Prophet would be raised above them after death; their sorrow, and the Prophet's sorrow, preceded the revelation.
rows.anchor: ما لنا منك إلا الدنيا، فإذا كانت الآخرة رفعت في الأعلى

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil describes an Ansari who longed for the Prophet when away and feared not seeing him in Paradise; after the Prophet died, the man prayed to be blinded until reunion, immediately became blind, and God joined him to the Prophet in Paradise.
rows.anchor: اللهم أعمني فلا أرى شيئا أبدا بعد حبيبي

rows.speaker: الكلبي وغيره
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi and others say obedience to God means observing obligations, while obedience to the Messenger means following the sunnah.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي وغيره: {ومن يطع الله} في الفرائض {والرسول} في السنن

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains فأولئك as the obedient people.
rows.anchor: قوله: {فأولئك} أي المطيعون. قاله الزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being with the blessed means enjoying the prophets' sight, visits, and company; their elevated rank does not mean the obedient cannot see them.
rows.anchor: فلا يتوهمن من أجل أنهم في أعلى عليين أنه لا يراهم

rows.speaker: ابن المظفر
rows.claim: Ibn al-Muzaffar defines the truthful as those who believe everything God commands without doubt and affirm the prophets, linking the term to 57:19.
rows.anchor: صدق بكل ما أمر الله، لا يتخالجه في شيء منه شك

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the truthful are the foremost Companions of the Prophet.
rows.anchor: الصديقون أفاضل أصحاب النبي

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the truthful were the first to affirm the prophets when they saw them.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: الصديقون [أول]

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj identifies the truthful as followers of the prophets.
rows.anchor: الصديقون أتباع الأنبياء

rows.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil identify the martyrs here as those killed in God's cause; al-Wahidi refers readers to his earlier discussion at 3:140.
rows.anchor: هم القتلى في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the martyrs are those who uphold justice.
rows.anchor: هم القائمون بالقسط

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the righteous are all other Muslims.
rows.anchor: هم سائر المسلمين

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the righteous are the people of Paradise.
rows.anchor: أهل الجنة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj understands “excellent companions” to refer to the prophets and these other blessed people as good company.
rows.anchor: أي حسن الأنبياء وهؤلاء رفيقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ordinary language, rafiq denotes gentleness of manner and action; a companion is called that because one benefits from company, and a traveling group is a rifqa because its members assist one another.
rows.anchor: في اللغة: لين الجانب ولطافة الفعل

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra explains singular رفيقا for a plural group by noting that rafiq, postman, and messenger can denote one or many; a plain noun like رجل cannot be used this way.
rows.anchor: وإنما وحد الرفيق وهو حقه الجمع؛ لأن الرفيق والبريد والرسول تذهب به العرب إلى الواحد وإلى الجمع

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says singulars can stand for a plural only when derived from a verb rather than being explicit nouns; he cites a poet's طاعم as evidence.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن تقول: حسن أولئك رجلا، وإنما يجوز ذلك إذا كان اسما مأخوذا من فعل

rows.speaker: شاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's line uses طاعم as evidence for al-Farra's grammatical rule; the source does not identify the poet.
rows.anchor: وإذا هم طعموا فألأم طاعم

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq argues that singulars can stand for plural groups in the accusative of specification, citing أجمل فتى and أحسنه as meaning the finest of the men.
rows.anchor: الواحد في التمييز ينوب عن الجماعة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra allows a singular to substitute for a plural only when it is an active participle, so he rejects the use of رجل for a plural group.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز حسن أولئك رجلا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj allows the singular construction and says it is also the doctrine of Sibawayh.
rows.anchor: وأجازه الزجاج كما ذكرنا، قال: وهو مذهب سيبويه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another interpretation means each blessed person is a good companion, as in 40:67, where people are brought out as infants.
rows.anchor: معنى قوله: {وحسن أولئك رفيقا} حسن كل واحد منهم رفيقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parsing makes رفيقا an accusative circumstantial expression: each of them is good as a companion.
rows.anchor: وانتصاب {رفيقا} على الحال، معنى: حسن كل منهم مرافقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent antecedent of the pronoun in “hold fast to Him” is God's name.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن الكناية في (به) تعود على اسم الله

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the pronoun refers to the light, meaning the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: الكناية تعود على النور الذي هو القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi says Ibn Jurayj's interpretation is close in meaning because holding fast to the Qur'an is holding fast to God.
rows.anchor: وهذا قريب من الأول في المعنى، لأن الاعتصام بالقرآن اعتصام بالله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses “hold fast to Him” as taking refuge in Him or making oneself secure through Him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: {واعتصموا به} يريد امتنعوا به

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: They explain holding fast to the Qur'an as protection from disobedience, and holding fast to God as protection from Satan's deviation and human desire through obedience and seeking His pleasure.
rows.anchor: الاعتصام بالقرآن: الامتناع به من معاصي الله، والاعتصام بالله: الامتناع به من زيغ الشيطان وهوى الإنسان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets God's mercy as Paradise and His favor as gifts beyond anything seen, heard, or describable.
rows.anchor: {وفضل} قال: يريد يتفضل عليهم بما لا عين رأت ولا أذن سمعت ولا ما يوصف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة والسدي
rows.claim: They explain “except what is recited to you” as the prohibited foods recited in the Qur'an, specifically the list in 5:3 from carrion through animals slaughtered at stone altars.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة والسدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: غير is accusative as a circumstantial expression modifying “made lawful to you,” like saying food is allowed without wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: انتصب (غير) على الحال من قوله تعالى: {أحلت لكم}

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra compares the construction to “allowed without excess or transgression”: when غير replaces لا, it takes the accusative construction that follows لا.
rows.anchor: فإذا جعلت (غير) مكان (لا)، صار النصب الذي بعد (لا) في (غير)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Livestock is permitted, but game is not lawful to hunt while one is in the consecrated state.
rows.anchor: أحلت لكم بهيمة الأنعام إلا أن تحلوا الصيد في حال الإحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular حرام and plural حرم mean people in the state of consecration.
rows.anchor: رجل حرام، وقوم حرم، أي: محرمون
